title: TSQueryBench: LLM-as-a-Judge for Time Series Explanations
abstract: arXiv:2604.02118v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Natural language explanations of time series data are increasingly produced by foundation models in high stakes domains, making factual correctness critical. Evaluating such explanations differs fundamentally from standard natural language generation: correctness requires verifying numerical claims against structured data rather than similarity to reference text. While LLM as a Judge has emerged as a scalable paradigm for text evaluation, its applicability to numerically grounded time series explanations remains unstudied. We introduce TSQueryBench, a controlled synthetic benchmark of 500 time series instances across 10 query types, each paired with correct, partially correct, and incorrect explanations. We evaluate six large language models across four tasks: explanation generation, relative ranking, independent scoring, and multi anomaly detection. translated_title: TSQueryBench：基于大语言模型作为裁判的时间序列解释评估
translated_abstract: 时间序列数据的自然语言解释越来越多地由基础模型在高风险领域生成，这使得事实正确性变得至关重要。评估此类解释与标准自然语言生成有根本不同：正确性要求对照结构化数据验证数值声明，而非与参考文本的相似性。虽然“大语言模型作为裁判”已成为文本评估的可扩展范式，但其在基于数值的时间序列解释中的适用性尚未被研究。我们引入了TSQueryBench，一个包含500个时间序列实例、覆盖10种查询类型的受控合成基准，每个实例配有正确、部分正确和不正确的解释。我们评估了六个大语言模型在四项任务上的表现：解释生成、相对排序、独立评分和多异常检测。我们的核心发现是一个一致的生成评估不对称性：生成能力较差的模型……
tldr: 本文提出了TSQueryBench基准，首次系统研究了大语言模型作为裁判在时间序列解释评估中的适用性，并揭示了生成与评估之间的不对称性这一关键发现。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces TSQueryBench, the first systematic study of LLM-as-a-Judge for evaluating time series explanations, revealing a key asymmetry between generation and evaluation capabilities.
